title: Neural interactions in the human frontal cortex dissociate reward and punishment learning (Combrisson et al., 2024): preprocessed SEEG high-gamma power, 16 patients (derivative)
description: Preprocessed stereotactic EEG (SEEG) high-gamma power from 16 patients with pharmaco-resistant focal epilepsy performing a probabilistic instrumental learning task with reward and punishment conditions. The derivative data cover bipolar derivations in anterior insula, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, lateral orbitofrontal cortex and ventromedial prefrontal cortex, time-locked to outcome at 256 Hz. The original study used information-theoretic analyses to identify separable reward and punishment subsystems in the frontal cortex.
methods_description: Depth iEEG was recorded with a Micromed system (512 or 1024 Hz) using Dixi electrodes, and bipolar derivations were computed between adjacent grey-matter contacts. Artifact- and spike-contaminated sites were removed by visual inspection. Gamma power (50-100 Hz) was estimated with a multitaper transform and down-sampled to 256 Hz. The article describes smoothing with a 10-point Savitzky-Golay filter, but the release does not state whether the released values include it. Patients performed a probabilistic instrumental learning task with reward and punishment cue pairs, and trial-wise prediction errors came from a Q-learning model.
